description:
Growing up is optional. Curiosity is not. 

Uncharted is a team on a mission to make space exploration feel like an adventure.

Inspired by the spirit of curiosity and imagination, I'm building an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer where young explorers learn through play, make meaningful decisions, and discover the science behind space missions using NASA resources.

Infinite imagination. A universe of possibilities.
summary:
A Leaf for Tomorrow is a browser-based educational card game developed by Team Uncharted for children aged 7–12, addressing NASA's Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge.

Inspired by NASA's research on growing plants in space, the game puts players in charge of a small greenhouse at a fictional Moon base. Players observe plant moisture, lighting, and airflow, then make decisions about watering, ventilation, lighting, and harvesting.

Through these decisions, players learn how space agriculture requires balancing limited water, energy, crew food, and scientific research while keeping plants growing for future harvests.

The game applies scientific principles from NASA's Veggie system, OSDR study OSD-269, and the VEG-03A lettuce experiment. Each decision produces visible consequences, helping children connect NASA's scientific knowledge with practical problem-solving.

Our goal is to turn real space-agriculture research into an engaging learning experience. The numerical rules are simplified for education rather than biological prediction.
details:
Project Overview

A Leaf for Tomorrow is an educational card game designed to help children aged 7–12 understand the challenges of growing food in space through interactive decision-making.

How It Works

Players manage three lettuce plants in a fictional lunar greenhouse across seven rounds.

They must observe plant conditions and make decisions about watering, LED lighting, ventilation, and harvesting.

The game provides limited resources: five water tokens, five energy tokens, and two care actions per round.

Players must balance three competing goals: feeding the crew, collecting a science sample, and keeping at least one plant growing.

Each round produces visible changes to the plants, allowing players to understand the consequences of their decisions.

NASA Scientific Knowledge

Our gameplay is inspired by NASA's Veggie system, OSDR study OSD-269, and the VEG-03A lettuce experiment.

We applied three main scientific concepts:

  • Root conditions: Plants need both water and oxygen, so players must avoid underwatering and overwatering.
  • Repeated harvesting: Players choose between harvesting some leaves now or harvesting the entire plant.
  • Food and research: Players decide how to distribute their harvest between crew consumption and scientific samples.

Lighting and ventilation also introduce environmental management decisions.

The scientific principles come from NASA research, while resource costs and growth scores are simplified educational rules.

Technology and Creativity

The game uses TypeScript to process player decisions, update plant conditions, and display results through an interactive web interface.

Its colorful card-based artwork makes scientific concepts accessible to younger learners.

AI tools assisted with artwork creation and coding. Our team designed the gameplay, integrated the components, and tested the mission.

Impact and Future Development

Our goal is to help children learn NASA science through experimentation and resource-management decisions.

The current version focuses on food production rather than complete lunar life-support systems.

Future development will include testing with children to evaluate learning outcomes and expanding the educational missions.
